import pathlib
base=pathlib.Path('/home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL0-prime-agent-luna6-low-fresh0/frozen/held-out-reference-2/play/users/u049/system/state/workspace/programs')

code='''def transform(grid):\n    out = [row[:] for row in grid]\n    # Extend the divider through the row separating matching blocks.\n    for r, row in enumerate(grid):\n        if not any(row):\n            above = next((grid[i] for i in range(r-1, -1, -1) if any(grid[i])), None)\n            below = next((grid[i] for i in range(r+1, len(grid)) if any(grid[i])), None)\n            if above is not None and below is not None and above == below:\n                out[r] = [3] * len(row)\n                break\n    return out\n'''

**Evaluating row matching issue**

I'm noticing an issue with the program when matching exact rows above and below, as it fails due to differing rows. I need to revise the approach to identify gaps within the bounding shape. The demo shows a row divider between horizontal bounds, but adjacent rows contain different components. I want to search for all-zero rows between any nonzero rows, specifically focusing on filling row 3 in this demo. I’ll simplify by looking at the first empty row bracketed by nonzero rows.

code='''def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    occupied = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if any(row)]
    for r in range(occupied[0] + 1, occupied[-1]):
        if not any(grid[r]):
            out[r] = [3] * len(grid[r])
            break
    return out
'''
p.write_text(code)
fn=__import__('runpy').run_path(str(p))['transform']
